headline: Build CLI tool scanning AI agent session transcripts (JSONL) for repeated-failure patterns: retry loops on same error, v
summary: Designed Phase 1 of CLI failure-pattern detector for AI agent transcripts. User has korean-prompt-compressor running long-term model training, needs non-competing side work. Used fight-clarify (two-agent perspective split), then fight-audit (sonnet proposer + opus auditor with real 599-session-file investigation + 20MB corpus analysis). Auditor's concrete measurements (reparse ~9ms, 275 subagent logs, 46% self-hook-noise baseline) disproved original real-time-hook justification; landed on Phase 1 = on-demand CLI scan. Design locked on: single flat Python script, cwd-based project identification, subagent-inclusive glob, extended fingerprint masking for truncation placeholders.
taskDescription: Build CLI tool scanning AI agent session transcripts (JSONL) for repeated-failure patterns: retry loops on same error, validation false-positives, no-progress sequences. First use case: Claude Code session logs. Future extensibility to Cursor / other agents via swappable parser boundary.
currentStatus: Design phase complete via audited decision process. Awaiting user confirmation ("이 방향으로 시작할까?") to green-light Phase 1 build. All 8 architecture decisions locked (on-demand vs real-time, Python + single-script, cwd-based grouping, subagent-inclusive glob, fingerprint masking, parser boundary design, rejected state-file approach for Phase 2). Zero files created yet — ready to initialize project directory + CLAUDE.md once confirmed.
keyDecisions: Decision: Phase 1 = on-demand CLI scan, NOT real-time hook — Reason: Auditor measured full-transcript reparse at 9ms-110ms; original cost justification was false; on-demand enables fast detector rule tuning by rerunning against saved transcripts
Decision: Implementation language = Python — Reason: Matches user's Windows CLAUDE.md convention (python, not python3; python3 is broken Store stub on this machine)

Decision: Design stays open to multiple agent formats long-term, implement Claude Code JSONL parser only now — Reason: YAGNI; parser boundary placed as swappable interface so Cursor parser can be added later without rewriting detectors

Decision: Start as single flat Python script, NOT a package (no pyproject.toml, no subpackages, no module splitting) — Reason: Auditor proved single 50-line stdlib script produces identical findings on 599 real transcripts in 5.1 seconds; module-splitting adds file-hopping cost per tuning without capability gain during early iteration

Decision: Identify project-ownership via cwd JSON field inside each transcript record, NOT via Claude Code's mangled-directory-name scheme — Reason: Mangling is lossy (folder collisions possible); cwd field is present in 100% of records and is lossless

Decision: Fingerprint/masking function must strip line numbers, absolute paths, hex hashes, timestamps, AND truncation placeholder tokens (toolu_* IDs, byte-count annotations) — Reason: Auditor found 18 real cases where identical errors repeat with different placeholder text; without masking, largest-output loops are silently missed

Decision: Phase 2 (future real-time hook) will NOT use incremental state file; instead reparse whole transcript + hook into PostToolUseFailure event — Reason: Reparse is cheap (9ms), state-file creates drift bugs (session resume/compaction can desync saved line numbers); PostToolUseFailure fires ~1/20th as often as PostToolUse, eliminating original latency concern

Decision: Session-file discovery must glob both ~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl (main transcripts) AND ~/.claude/projects/*/*/subagents/*.jsonl (subagent transcripts) — Reason: Original proposal missed subagent logs; auditor found 275 real subagent files, accounting for ~7% of repeat-failure hits
failedApproaches: Approach: Build real-time PostToolUse hook as Phase 1 → Result: Auditor's actual measurements (9ms reparse cost, PostToolUseFailure event exists and fires rarely) disproved both justifications (stateless-hook-needs-persisted-state false, real-time-causes-latency false) → Lesson: Verify performance/architecture assumptions against real measurements before letting them drive build-order; don't trust 'hooks are stateless so we need external state' as self-evidently true

Approach: Multi-file Python package structure (pyproject.toml + detectors/ submodule + windowing.py + report.py) as Phase 1 foundation → Result: Auditor showed single 50-line stdlib script produces identical findings on same 599 real transcripts in 5.1 seconds → Lesson: For rule-tuning-heavy tool in early iteration, module-splitting adds per-change file-hopping cost without adding capability; defer structure until logic outgrows what one file can hold

Approach: Reconstruct Claude Code's cwd-to-mangled-directory-name algorithm to identify project ownership → Result: Mangling is lossy (folder name collisions possible) and unnecessary since every record carries exact cwd field → Lesson: Prefer reading already-present exact field over reverse-engineering lossy derived one
